prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1336; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into her lane while turning. Airbags did not deploy. Insured states she was taken by ambulance to the emergency department and has a suspected wrist fracture. Assigned to adjuster for liability and injury review. Requested police report number and photos of both vehicles.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's side regarding the bodily injury portion. Claimant confirms a fractured wrist diagnosed in the emergency department, now in a splint with orthopedic follow-up scheduled. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says she is handling the matter directly. Explained the claims process, the bodily injury evaluation steps, and that medical records and billing statements will be needed before any settlement discussion.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer noted both drivers' statements conflict on who had the right of way, with a witness statement supporting the claimant's account of a left-turn conflict. Property damage photos show front-end damage to both vehicles consistent with a low-speed impact. No citations issued at scene. Liability leaning toward the other driver pending the witness interview.

Entry 4: Received medical authorization form and initial treatment records from the claimant. Records confirm a closed fracture of the distal radius, treated with a splint and a follow-up visit with an orthopedic specialist. Requested complete billing records and the orthopedic consult notes. Contacted the other driver's carrier to place them on notice of the claim and request their insured's recorded statement.

Entry 5: Other carrier confirmed liability is disputed and will reserve rights pending their insured's statement. Scheduled a follow-up call with the claimant to check on treatment progress and to remind her to forward the orthopedic records once received. Reserve set for the bodily injury and property damage exposures. File remains open, with the next review set after the specialist visit and the witness interview are complete.
